Define a text style

Source: R/style.R
text_style.Rd

A text style lists only the properties it changes. Anything left `NULL` is inherited from `base` (a theme role name or another text style), or from the role the component uses by default. So `text_style(weight = 600)` passed to [bb_text()] means "body text, semibold", and the same style passed as a table header style means "table header, semibold".

Usage

text_style(
  base = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  italic = NULL,
  lineheight = NULL,
  case = NULL
)

Arguments

base

A theme role name (e.g. `"note"`) or another `text_style()` to inherit from.

size

Font size in points.

weight

Font weight, numeric (100-900) or a name (`"regular"`, `"semibold"`, `"bold"`, ...).

color

Text colour: an R colour or a theme colour name.

family

Font family.

italic

`TRUE` for italic.

lineheight

Line height as a multiple of the font size.

case

Letter case applied to plain text: `"none"`, `"upper"`, `"lower"` or `"title"`.

Value

A `bb_text_style` object.

Details

**Weights.** `weight` takes a number (100-900) or a name such as `"semibold"`. 400 and 700 use the family's regular and bold faces. Other weights are looked up with systemfonts: if a face with that weight is installed (for example "Source Sans 3 Semibold"), its family name is used, which `cairo_pdf()` resolves through fontconfig. Otherwise bodybuildr falls back to bold (600 and above) or regular, with a one-time message.

Examples

text_style(size = 12, weight = "semibold", color = "muted")
#> <text_style> 
#>  size: 12
#>  weight: 600
#>  color: muted
text_style("note", italic = TRUE)
#> <text_style> base: note 
#>  italic: TRUE
